summary:
Settings now has the Papier look. At the top there is the title and four chips: Profile, Security, Assistants and Workspace. Each group is one white sheet of rows, with the label on the left, the value or field in the middle and the action on the right.

- **Profile:** a header with your photo, your name, your role and the company. Below it: name, email, About you, language and theme. When you change something, a black "Save" pill appears next to the title. After saving, the pill says "Saved" for a moment and your name is briefly highlighted. Mistakes show in red under the field concerned. "Delete my account" is a quiet link under the sheet.
- **Security:** two rows, Password and Two-factor (shown as On or Off). Each opens a side panel. The password panel checks your input before sending it and warns that your other sessions will be signed out. The two-factor panel shows a real QR code and the backup codes. While the codes or the key are on screen, the panel cannot be closed by accident.
- **Assistants:** a "Connected" heading with a count, then one card per computer, assistant or token. A card's panel shows its details, with Disconnect or Revoke confirmed inside the panel itself. Below that, an "Add" row of four tiles: Computer, Assistant, Token and Browser extension. Each tile opens its panel with the install command, the MCP address and the client list, or the extension steps. A new token is shown once in a panel that cannot be closed by mistake. The new card then appears with a short highlight.
- **Workspace:** the organization's initial in a black square, then the owner. Admins also get rows for company SSO (Not set up / On / pending, plus a panel with DNS verification and removal confirmed in place), the managers switch with its legal sentence, and team repositories ("None selected" in red, plus a panel to tick or add repos). Only the owner sees "Delete the organization" under the sheet.

Members, invitations, groups and the directory import are no longer shown here. The old links #membres, #organigramme and #groupes, and the directory-import return address (?annuaire=…), now go to Team.
kept: Name change: Profile sheet, Name row, server updateProfileAction. It now also refreshes the whole layout, so the sidebar name updates too (tested).
Email shown: Profile sheet, Email row.
About you, with length limit, hint and counter near the limit: Profile sheet, About row, updateAboutAction. The cursor goes there when you arrive by /reglages#profil.
Interface language: Profile sheet, Language row. setLocaleAction is still in actions.ts (the site footer and onboarding use it).
Theme, light and dark: Profile sheet, Theme row (useTheme).
Change password, with length, mismatch and wrong-password refusals and the 'others signed out' message: Security sheet, Password panel.
Two-factor on and off, real QR code, manual key, code check, backup codes shown once and regenerated: Security sheet, Two-factor panel. The steps showing secrets are locked.

Delete my account, with every branch (sole member deletes the organization too, choosing a successor, password, 2FA code, typed word, server refusals per field, redirect to /connexion?supprime=compte): side panel under the Profile sheet.
Delete the organization, owner only (password, 2FA, typed word, redirect to /connexion?supprime=organisation): side panel under the Workspace sheet.
Computers: card plus panel (connected date, last used, note), Disconnect confirmed in place. Install command, 'Ask Claude' copy and /documentation link: Add > Computer panel.
Assistants (MCP): card plus panel (client, host, dates), Disconnect confirmed in place. MCP address and the ClaudeAi/ChatGPT/Claude Code/Codex/Cursor instructions: Add > Assistant panel.
Personal tokens: card plus panel (hint, created, last used or 'never used'), Revoke confirmed in place. Creation with the secret shown once, a copy button and a warning: Add > Token panel, locked.
Browser extension (Ask Claude prompt, 3 steps, server address and variable): Add > Extension panel. Step 3 opens the token panel.

Anchors from Connections and onboarding: #ordinateurs, #assistants and #extension open the right panel; #jetons, #sso, #managers, #depots-equipe and #equipe open the right group (tested in settings-tabs.test.ts).
Company SSO (register OIDC/SAML, status, DNS record with copy buttons, verify with 'not yet' notice and success toast, remove confirmed in place): Workspace sheet, SSO row and panel.
Managers switch with the legal sentence, optimistic with a failure toast: Workspace sheet, Managers row.
Team repositories (warning when none, checkboxes, add a repo, withUnchecked kept and exported): Workspace sheet, Repositories row and panel.
Owner(s) of the organization: Workspace sheet, Owner row.

Members, invitations, groups and directory import: no longer drawn here. The old anchors #membres, #organigramme and #groupes and /reglages?annuaire=… redirect to /equipe (page.test.ts). members.tsx, groups.tsx and annuaire.tsx were left untouched.
Token split rules (manual / computer with its prefix removed / assistant with a live refresh): page.tsx, unchanged and still tested in page.test.ts.

leastSure: I accidentally flipped the shared managers switch off (a 'text=Manage' target matched the 'Managers' label). When checked afterwards as Claire, the switch was on ('true') and the screenshots show it on, so it looks restored. I can't be sure whether the toggle failed or something else turned it back on.

Sign-in as david@essai.leon.local was refused once (saved session expired, one password try, refused). That account may be blocked for about 15 minutes; everything after that ran as claire and karim. I briefly printed the demo README line holding SHOOT_PASSWORD in my own tool output by mistake; nothing was written to the repo.
The Save pill sits in the page header and is not sticky. At 771px high, if Profile scrolls (for example a long About), the pill can go under the top bar, though the form still saves with Enter.
The 2FA code, backup-code and SSO 'verified' paths were checked in code and by opening the panels, not run end to end: that would need a real authenticator and DNS, and it changes shared accounts.

The prototype uses square photos and a caption under the organization name. I kept the kit's round photos, to match the real sidebar, and left the organization caption empty because there is no real data for it.
